facts.statement: Only RackCad.Plugin references AutoCAD. UI, Application and Domain have no Autodesk references, and UI does not reference Plugin, so no WPF window or pure builder can write to the Database.
facts.evidence: src/RackCad.Plugin/RackCad.Plugin.csproj:12,29-37 (AutoCAD.NET, AcCoreMgd, AcDbMgd, AcMgd); src/RackCad.UI/RackCad.UI.csproj:7-8 (Domain and Application only); src/RackCad.Application/RackCad.Application.csproj:6; grep 'Autodesk' over src/**/*.cs outside Plugin returns 0 hits.

facts.statement: Three commands reach the Selective creation chain, all through DrawSelectiveViewFromAuthored: (1) RACKSELECTIVO and its alias RS; (2) RACKCAD and its alias RK, via the SelectiveInsertionRequest case; (3) RACKEDITAR and its alias RED, via SelectiveKindHandler.Edit -> EditSelective, in the non-UpdateOnly ('Insertar') branch. Entry (3) reaches the same mutation sites. It differs only in its inputs: id = embed.Id, source = embed, and the authored JSON comes from the reconciler.

Each invocation creates exactly one view. For the frontal, one fondo is chosen with editor.GetInteger when fondoCount > 1, and this happens before any DB write. The planta is a separate branch. On RACKEDITAR 'Insertar', the redraws, renames, phantom erases and the Regen of the existing views all commit BEFORE the new view is created.
The library import runs INSIDE the creation callee: CreateBlock takes the document lock, calls EnsureForPlan, and only then opens T_create. The int result is discarded.

WblockCloneObjects runs with no RackCad transaction open on the destination drawing: the presence-check transaction committed at :79 and the side-DB transaction committed at :114. It runs before T_create exists, so a rollback of T_create cannot undo it.
facts.evidence: src/RackCad.Plugin/Drawing/BlockLibraryImporter.cs:68-80,103-115,122-123; src/RackCad.Plugin/Systems/Shared/SystemBlockWriter.cs:25-27; the comment at src/RackCad.Plugin/Systems/Shared/ViewBlockDraw.cs:59-64 states the import 'mutates the database on its own account'

facts.statement: The library side DB is opened by the importer itself, from the SHARED configured path (a user-settings override, else the default), with OpenForReadAndAllShare. It is kept in a process-wide static cache keyed by path + LastWriteTimeUtc + Length. No private copy is made, and the caller does not supply the Database.

Every importer outcome collapses to an int, and the post-import Found/Missing facts are discarded. Cases:
- 0 for a null db or plan (:27-30).
- 0 when no names are wanted (:62-65) or none are missing (:82-85).
- 0 when the file is absent (:88-91) or Acquire returns null (:97-100).
- 0 when none of the names are in the library (:117-120).
- 0 when an exception is swallowed (:126-131).
- On success it returns the REQUESTED id count, which is not verified (:124).
- ImportAdapter always reports WasAttempted=true (:140-141).

T_create holds every definition-content write and the envelope write, and it commits internally. No Abort exists. An exception inside T_create leaves through the using-Dispose without a Commit and is converted into a Failure result.

The envelope is skipped SILENTLY when the payload is null or empty. That happens when the design is null (SerializeSelectiveDesign) or the JSON is empty (WrapSelectivePayload). The create path never reads the envelope back.

On the create path only the new-Xrecord branch of RackBlockData.Write can run. The definition is a BlockTableRecord created in the same transaction, and its extension dictionary is created in the same call. The overwrite branch (existing.Data = buffer) is therefore not reached on create. This assumes the host behaviour that a new object has no extension dictionary and that a new dictionary is empty.

Placement opens a SECOND lock and transaction (T_place) after T_create has committed, and runs editor.Drag inside them. The jig sets only Position on the top-level BlockReference. No Layer, Rotation, ScaleFactors, Normal, dynamic property or RecordGraphicsModified is set on it. T_place commits internally. Nothing consumes the returned PlacedId.
facts.evidence: src/RackCad.Plugin/Drawing/BlockPlacement.cs:179-199, 240-244 (Position :242); grep PlacedId: set only at src/RackCad.Plugin/Drawing/BlockPlacement.cs:46 and src/RackCad.Plugin/Drawing/LateralHeaderDrawService.cs:186, declared at :323

facts.statement: Any non-OK Drag result takes the cancel path. That includes Enter, because NullResponseAccepted makes the Sampler return Cancel. The cancel path disposes the non-resident reference, commits T_place empty, and then runs a compensating erase of the committed view definition (new lock plus T_cleanup) followed by T_purge.

Neither review stated this. The purge candidate list on cancel holds the BlockTableRecord of EVERY BlockReference directly inside the view definition, not only the private ARRAY header definitions. Loose catalog pieces are appended directly into the view definition, for example the planta largueros, separadores, topes and safety items, and frontal singletons. Their catalog definitions are therefore purge candidates too. The XML doc at :120-122 describes only the 'private nested header defs'.

Consequence of F-13: a cancelled jig can erase library definitions that this same command just imported with WblockCloneObjects. It can also erase PRE-EXISTING catalog definitions that have no other reference in the drawing, because Database.Purge keeps only zero-reference ids and the code then erases them. The actual extent depends on host Purge semantics.
The cancel cleanup does not collect the anonymous dimension blocks of RotatedDimensions. The redefine path does collect them (DimBlockId), so on cancel those blocks are left orphaned.
If PlaceBlockWithJig throws, PlaceAndReport returns Failure. The enveloped definition committed by T_create stays in the drawing, because the erase runs only when placedId.IsNull.
The creation path never regenerates: ViewBlockDraw.DrawAndPlace, CreateBlock and PlaceAndReport do not call ApplyRegen or Editor.Regen.

Across the Plugin:
- There is no Transaction.Abort() call.
- The only StartOpenCloseTransaction is LateralHeaderDrawService.cs:278, on the redraw path.
- There is no '.Normal =', BlockTransform or SetDatabaseDefaults call.
- The only TransformBy is on a Vector3d in RackDuplicarCommands.cs:147.

Effective names are UniqueBlockName(SanitizeBlockName(requested)) with an _n suffix, probed against the LIVE block table inside the transaction. Nested ARRAY names restart per plan: SEL_FRONTAL_<Role>_<i> with i from 0, and PLANTA_CAB_<n> numbered within the plan. If K frontals were created in one T_M, every fondo would request identical nested names, so their suffixes would depend on creation order. Nested effective names are never returned; only the view name is.

An empty effective view name is NOT reachable on the Selective frontal and planta paths. SanitizeBlockName can return '' for input made only of invalid characters. However, a frontal name that sanitizes to blank falls back to the default 'Selectivo frontal - N frentes - H..' name, and the planta name always carries the ' - planta' suffix. Review B's CR-12 empty-name hazard does not apply to these two paths.

The Plugin never mints a Selective id. The id comes from one of two places:
- the UI session, which calls Identity.EnsureId -> Guid.NewGuid and exposes it as window.RackId;
- embed.Id on RACKEDITAR.
No check exists that sibling envelopes carry the same id.

RackDefinitionCreator.CreateInTransaction has no caller in src/; its only references are tests. At this SHA it has four relevant properties:
- It checks TopTransaction.UnmanagedObject.
- It refuses an envelope whose Name is blank.
- It serializes the RackEmbedDocument itself.
- It reads the envelope back and compares ordinally.
The Selective path composes the envelope with the name as given, and a blank name is allowed there.

Dimensions default to None in the domain, and EffectiveDetail maps None to None. The annotation toggles NumberFronts, NumberLevels and DrawRackName are bool auto-properties with no initializer, so false by default. As a result, the dimension and annotation writes, including the layers RACKCAD_COTAS and RACKCAD_ANOTACIONES, occur only when the user enables them. The UI defaults were not checked.

Negative scale occurs only on NESTED piece references. Examples are the planta largueros built with mirrored:true, and the grouper prototypes, which keep MirroredX/Y. The ARRAY placement references in the view definition are always built with mirrored:false for Selective.

The lateral branch starts from the same entry points but is outside the frontal/planta seam. It keeps its own lock, import, transaction and Commit, and it reuses CreateSystemBlock, RackBlockData.Write and PlaceAndReport.

limitations: This was a static reading of the extract at scratchpad/main2 only. Nothing was compiled or executed, and nothing was observed in AutoCAD.

The seam contract (SL-1..SL-6, T_M, PREPARE-W) is not present in the extract: docs/adr has no mention of it. I adjudicated the required operations only against the clause fragments quoted in the two reviews, so R-01, R-06 conformance, R-14 and R-21 remain UNCERTAIN.

The fresh sweep was a grep of mutating AutoCAD APIs over the 15 Plugin files on the chain, plus event, overrule and reflection greps over the whole Plugin. The UI was excluded by construction, because it has no Autodesk references and no reference to Plugin.
UI default values for the annotation and dimension toggles were not checked. Only the domain defaults were read (SelectiveRackSystem, SelectivePalletDesign).

Builder internals were read only far enough to settle grouping, mirroring, loose-instance membership and the dimension and annotation gates. Safety-item placement (SelectiveSafetyPlacement, SelectiveDesviadorDrawing) was not traced beyond the fact that it appends to the loose list.
F-14 (erasure of catalog definitions on cancel) depends on host Database.Purge semantics. The collection of those candidates is a FACT; the erase outcome is UNCERTAIN.
The line numbers the reviews cited were spot-checked, not all re-verified. Every citation used in this report was read directly.
